draft.title: Developing the business concept
card: A business concept is a clear description of the business idea. It turns a gap or opportunity in the market into something that can be sold.
Product
what the business will sell, whether a good or a service.
Target market
the group of customers the business aims to serve, such as students or busy parents.
Reason to choose
why customers would buy from this business instead of another, such as lower price, better quality or more convenience.
draft.remember: A concept says what is sold, to whom, and why customers would choose it.

a.q: Which statement is a clear business concept?
opts: Fresh healthy lunches delivered to Geelong office workers
A business that wants to make a lot of money in food
A café with a lease on a corner shop in Geelong
Healthy lunches for sale at a price that covers costs
a.why: It says what is sold (healthy lunches), to whom (Geelong office workers) and gives a reason to choose it (fresh and delivered). The lease option names a place but not who the customers are or why they would buy.
a.clue: Look for the option that names a product, a customer group and a reason to buy.

b.q: Priya plans a bike repair service in Ballarat. She says it will fix all bikes for everyone at fair prices. Which change would best improve her concept?
opts: Aim at students and offer repairs at their school
Lower her prices so that they are cheaper than any rival
Add car repairs so that more people can be customers
Choose a business name before she plans anything else
b.why: Her idea names a product but has no clear target market or reason to choose her. Naming students and a convenient school service fixes both. Lowering prices gives a reason to choose but still leaves out who the customers are.
b.clue: Which part of the concept is missing: what, to whom or why?

a.best: Fresh healthy lunches delivered to Geelong office workers

b.best: Aim at students and offer repairs at their school

problems.detail: Why (b) says Priya's idea has no clear reason to choose her, but she does offer 'fair prices', and the card lists price as a reason to choose. The why should say her reason is weak or vague, not missing. As written it could confuse students who notice the price reason.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear correct answer that matches the card. One minor issue: why (b) says Priya gives no reason to choose her, though 'fair prices' is a reason, just a weak one.
